title: Boosting Task Scheduling Data Locality with Low-latency, HW-accelerated Label Propagation
problem: Hardware-accelerated task schedulers dispatch ready tasks to the first available core without locality awareness, causing cache misses when dependent tasks execute on different cores. Existing locality-aware policies require static programmer hints or incur high scheduling overhead incompatible with fine-grained tasks.
motivation: Fine-grained task-parallel workloads on many-core systems suffer from data cache misses that negate parallelism gains because conventional task schedulers ignore data dependency graphs when making placement decisions.
method: Task-LP adds a hardware accelerator that clusters up to 128 in-flight tasks using label propagation—an algorithm where each task adopts the most common group label among dependent tasks. For speed, it stores task dependencies as compact binary data and uses bitwise operations, converging in under 300 cycles for typical task graphs. The Task Placement Engine then uses these clusters to assign tasks to cores, tuning the balance between keeping related tasks on the same core (so they share cached data) and spreading work evenly across available cores. The system runs on a 24-core RISC-V processor (Rocket Chip) prototyped on an FPGA (Alveo U55C).
key_novelty: A dedicated hardware accelerator that runs label propagation to cluster task dependencies in under 300 cycles—up to 581x faster than software—enabling locality-aware task placement without slowing down scheduling.
contributions: Task-LP: a parametrized HW label-propagation accelerator clustering 128-node task graphs in under 600 cycles, synthesized at 0.313 mm2 in GF 12 nm
Task Placement Engine (TPE) combining LP cluster labels and core-idleness status via a single tunable relaxation parameter
Demonstration of up to 1.50x execution-time improvement and 1.81x average task-size reduction on a 24-core RISC-V FPGA system
Clustering quality shown statistically indistinguishable from software LP while being up to 581x faster

metrics.speedup: up to 1.50x program execution time improvement on 24 cores
metrics.area: 0.313 mm2 at GF 12 nm for 128-node Task-LP configuration
metrics.ppa: 600+ MHz timing met in ASIC synthesis
metrics.accuracy: clustering modularity statistically indistinguishable from software LP
metrics.other: LP accelerator 581x faster than equivalent software LP; task size reduction up to 1.81x

baselines: Random Task Stealing (GNU OpenMP / Nanos baseline)
limitations: The 128-node context window limits visibility of long-range task dependencies; larger windows grow area super-linearly (~N^1.58), and gains diminish for compute-bound workloads where random placement already achieves high core utilization.
